summary: Pioneer Base is a free browser game where kids aged 7 to 12 run a lunar or Martian outpost for 30 mission days and keep four astronauts safe. Every day the player splits limited power between life support, food and science, decides whether to build shielding or more solar panels, and chooses whether to shelter from a solar storm or keep working. A live preview shows what each plan will do before the day runs, so no choice is free. The numbers come from NASA sources: real solar storm dates from DONKI, radiation measured by the Curiosity rover, crew oxygen and food needs, the 15-day lunar night and the radio delay to Earth. When the mission ends, the game shows the exact chain of decisions that made it fail or succeed, and every value is tagged Real, Derived or Simplified with its source. A bonus 3D version adds an explorable base and a Hard mode where the crew drives a rover to the outpost and solves chemistry and physics challenges on the way.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Pioneer Base is a turn-based survival game: one turn is one mission day, and a full game takes 8 to 12 minutes. The player chooses the Moon (a 15-day night with no solar power, strong radiation) or Mars (dust on the panels, a dust storm, thin sunlight). Each day they switch systems on or off, choose the crew activity (Science, Maintenance or Shelter) and the food rations, and spend 14 supply crates that never come back. When power is short, systems shut down one by one, so the player sees one shortage cause the next.

THE TRADE-OFFS (no safe choice)

- Power: cheap solar panels or a reactor that works at night.

- Radiation: shield layers or more useful modules; shelter in a solar storm or do science.

- Life support: making oxygen costs power, and on the Moon it also costs water.

- Food: grow crops in a greenhouse, or eat smaller rations and lose health.

- Communication delay: a radio message takes about 1.3 seconds from the Moon but 3 to 22 minutes from Mars, so in an emergency the crew must decide alone.

HOW WE USED NASA DATA

Every number is in one data file and is tagged Real (measured or published), Derived (calculated from real values) or Simplified (a game value, chosen on purpose). Real values are never changed to make the game easier. The panel "Where do these numbers come from?" lists every value with a plain explanation and a NASA link. Examples: two real solar storms from NASA DONKI (11 May 2024 and 3 October 2024) set the storm days; Curiosity measured 0.67 mSv per day on Mars; four astronauts need 3.36 kg of oxygen a day; sunlight at Mars is 1 / 1.524 squared = 43% of the Moon's; the radio delay comes from the NASA Moon and Mars fact sheets. The DONKI dates are stored in the game, not live, and the game says so.

WHY IT IS DIFFERENT

1. A cause-chain debrief: at the end, the game rebuilds what happened from the real log of that game (for example: the lunar night began, no reactor, the battery emptied, the oxygen plant shut down, the crew was evacuated), names the trade-off and gives one thing to try next time.

2. Tested balance: automatic tests play 200 games per site. A player who does nothing always fails, a careful but imperfect player wins about half the time on the Moon, an expert nearly always wins.

3. Made for kids and classrooms: no install, no account, works on phones and laptops, keyboard support, and a built-in 45-minute teacher guide. Failure is always an "evacuation", never worse, and six Myth or Reality cards teach real facts with sources.

BONUS: 3D VERSION

The same simulation engine, ported to C# in Unity: a third-person base you can walk around, true skies (black on the Moon, butterscotch on Mars), a companion drone called PIP that explains the real numbers, and a Hard mode where the ship crashes 40 km from the outpost. The player drives a pressurized rover, camps to recharge, and opens supply pods by solving 13 chemistry and physics challenges (electrolysis of water, energy = power x time, radio delay, shielding). Play it at https://ashraf20i.github.io/pioneer-base/play3d/

TOOLS

Web game: HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no framework and no external files; the engine is tested in Node. 3D version: Unity 2021.3 (C#), exported to WebGL; every model, texture and sound is generated by our own code. Source code: https://github.com/Ashraf20i/pioneer-base

IMPACT

Students aged 7 to 12 learn by playing, failing and trying again that a choice made today has a cost tomorrow, which is what real mission planners face every day.
